correctness.reference: Each changed layout matches all 74 generic and 112 older benchmark captures from the prior candidate exactly, including output metadata and physical plans. The alignment-16 roundtrip is byte-identical to that candidate. No fresh Spark comparison, planner compilation, Arrow unit-test run or full 6332-observation replay is needed for this diagnostic relink; the Rust code is unchanged.

code_placement.method: Input object sections have identical payloads, symbols, relocations and attributes except the one selected section alignment. All other archive members are byte-identical. Relinked loop instructions are compared after resolving named relocations. Full normalized instruction text is retained in the preceding artifact.
code_placement.observation: The baseline, alignment-128 and alignment-256 binaries place the two hot inner loops in the same 4 KiB virtual page. Original, alignment-32 and alignment-64 split them across a page boundary. Alignment 128 still leaves the function prologue in the preceding page. Code placement changes elsewhere in the binary can also result from relinking.

performance.method: Sequential release execution timings on CPU 2, 1048576 rows in 8192-row batches. Two warmups and nine execution samples per fresh process. Sixteen randomized, balanced before/after pairs per comparison; eight pairs per identical-executable control. Report medians of process medians. Execution-only perf counters are phase-gated and fully scheduled. Bootstrap intervals resample whole process pairs, not individual samples. Builds, checks and code inspection finish before each measurement group; no builds, tests, profiles or other timings run concurrently.

performance.interpretation: Changing the target section alignment to 128 or 256 reduces the original candidate control by about 2.3%, whereas 32 and 64 improve it by less than 0.4%. The alignment-256 candidate matches the accepted baseline within 0.06% in this series and preserves the selected add-zero gains. This is direct evidence that the observed gap is sensitive to linked code placement; it is not evidence that the unchanged control query performs additional Spark normalization work.

limitations: No portable runtime fix or source alignment attribute is introduced. The experiment targets one compiler-generated symbol from one build on one AMD Ryzen 7 8845HS core. Future compiler, feature, dependency and binding builds can place code differently.

The target section alignment can also shift later code and data. Correlation with the inner loops sharing a page does not identify the exact processor mechanism, instruction-cache behavior, translation behavior or branch-predictor cause.

The hashing source and seeding policy remain unchanged, but individual random hash seeds are not fixed or captured. This study does not separately isolate every contribution of seed distribution from code placement.
The original-to-alignment-256 branch-miss counter drops about 7.68% in the normal series. That correlation alone does not prove a branch-predictor cause.

Identical-original and identical-alignment-256 overall medians differ by -0.21% and -0.22%. Small control variation remains; the selected approximately 2.3% layout effect is larger than these same-executable comparisons.

Six selected pre-existing controls lie between -0.11% and +0.15% versus the accepted baseline in this run. This is bounded control coverage, not a claim that every earlier performance difference has vanished.

The 744 captures are repeated benchmark observations from four layouts, not new unique Spark corpus coverage. No new Spark reference is generated. Existing 331 raw Spark differences, other workloads, batch sizes, planning latency and Delta I/O remain outside this experiment.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import hashlib
import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

p = Path(__file__).parent
directory = p / 'link-inputs'
directory.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
args = sys.argv[1:]
inputs = {}
for i, arg in enumerate(args):
    file = Path(arg)
    if arg.endswith('.o') and file.is_file():
        digest = hashlib.sha256(file.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
        copy = directory / (digest[:12] + '-' + file.name)
        shutil.copy2(file, copy)
        inputs[arg] = {'path': str(copy), 'sha256': digest}
        args[i] = str(copy)
command = ['cc', *args]
(p / 'link-command.json').write_text(json.dumps({'cwd': os.getcwd(), 'command': command, 'objects': inputs}, indent=2) + '\n')
sys.exit(subprocess.run(command).returncode)

import hashlib
import json
import shutil
import struct
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

p = Path(__file__).parent
spec = json.loads((p / 'target-symbol.json').read_text())
original = Path(spec['library'])
link = json.loads((p / 'link-command.json').read_text())
sha = lambda file: hashlib.sha256(Path(file).read_bytes()).hexdigest()

def sections(file):
    data = Path(file).read_bytes()
    assert data[:6] == b'\x7fELF\x02\x01'
    start = struct.unpack_from('<Q', data, 0x28)[0]
    size, count, names_id = struct.unpack_from('<HHH', data, 0x3a)
    headers = [struct.unpack_from('<IIQQQQIIQQ', data, start + i * size) for i in range(count)]
    names = data[headers[names_id][4]:headers[names_id][4] + headers[names_id][5]]
    result = {}
    for h in headers:
        name = names[h[0]:].split(b'\0', 1)[0].decode()
        result[name] = {'kind': h[1], 'flags': h[2], 'address': h[3], 'size': h[5],
                        'link': h[6], 'info': h[7], 'alignment': h[8], 'entry_size': h[9],
                        'data': data[h[4]:h[4] + h[5]] if h[1] != 8 else b''}
    return result

old_sections = sections(p / 'original.o')
assert old_sections[spec['section']]['alignment'] == 16
members = subprocess.check_output(['ar', 't', str(original)], text=True).splitlines()
original_members = {name: hashlib.sha256(subprocess.check_output(['ar', 'p', str(original), name])).hexdigest() for name in members}
record = json.loads((p / 'relink-builds.json').read_text()) if (p / 'relink-builds.json').exists() else {'original_library': {'path': str(original), 'sha256': sha(original)}, 'variants': {}}
for alignment in [int(x) for x in sys.argv[1:]] or [16, 32, 64, 128, 256]:
    directory = p / f'align{alignment}'
    directory.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    obj = directory / spec['object_member']
    command = ['llvm-objcopy', '--set-section-alignment', f'{spec["section"]}={alignment}', str(p / 'original.o'), str(obj)]
    subprocess.run(command, check=True)
    new_sections = sections(obj)
    assert new_sections.keys() == old_sections.keys()
    for name, section in old_sections.items():
        expected = section | ({'alignment': alignment} if name == spec['section'] else {})
        assert new_sections[name] == expected, name
    archive = directory / original.name
    shutil.copy2(original, archive)
    subprocess.run(['ar', 'rD', str(archive), str(obj)], check=True, capture_output=True)
    assert subprocess.check_output(['ar', 't', str(archive)], text=True).splitlines() == members
    for name, digest in original_members.items():
        member_digest = hashlib.sha256(subprocess.check_output(['ar', 'p', str(archive), name])).hexdigest()
        assert member_digest == (sha(obj) if name == spec['object_member'] else digest), name
    args = link['command'].copy()
    assert args.count(str(original)) == 1
    args[args.index(str(original))] = str(archive)
    args[args.index('-o') + 1] = str(directory / 'bench')
    with (directory / 'link.log').open('w') as log:
        subprocess.run(args, cwd=link['cwd'], stdout=log, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, check=True)
    symbols = subprocess.check_output(['nm', '-SC', '--defined-only', str(directory / 'bench')], text=True)
    matches = [line.split(maxsplit=3) for line in symbols.splitlines() if line.endswith(' ' + spec['demangled'])]
    assert len(matches) == 1
    address = int(matches[0][0], 16)
    assert address % alignment == 0
    record['variants'][str(alignment)] = {
        'objcopy_command': command, 'link_command': args,
        'object_sha256': sha(obj), 'archive_sha256': sha(archive), 'binary_sha256': sha(directory / 'bench'),
        'hot_loop_address': hex(address), 'alignment_mod64': address % 64,
        'only_selected_section_alignment_changed': True, 'other_archive_members_identical': True,
    }
    print(alignment, hex(address), sha(directory / 'bench'), flush=True)
assert record['variants']['16']['binary_sha256'] == sha(p / 'control-bench')
assert sha(original) == record['original_library']['sha256']
(p / 'relink-builds.json').write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2) + '\n')

import hashlib
import json
import mmap
import re
import struct
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

p = Path(__file__).parent
q = p.parent / 'float-in-zero-bool-a651e99'
choices = {'before': q / 'before-bench', 'after': p / 'control-bench', 'align32': p / 'align32/bench', 'align64': p / 'align64/bench', 'align128': p / 'align128/bench', 'align256': p / 'align256/bench'}
top = json.loads((p / 'target-symbol.json').read_text())['demangled']
selected = [top]
records = [{'name': name} for name in selected]
sha = lambda data: hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
for variant in choices:
    binary = choices[variant]
    symbols = subprocess.check_output(['nm', '-SC', '--defined-only', str(binary)], text=True)
    (p / f'{variant}-symbols.txt').write_text(symbols)
    rows = [row for line in symbols.splitlines() if len(row := line.split(maxsplit=3)) == 4]
    names = {int(row[0], 16): row[3] for row in rows if int(row[0], 16) != 0}
    with binary.open('rb') as file, mmap.mmap(file.fileno(), 0, access=mmap.ACCESS_READ) as elf:
        assert elf[:6] == b'\x7fELF\x02\x01'
        section_offset = struct.unpack_from('<Q', elf, 0x28)[0]
        section_size, section_count = struct.unpack_from('<HH', elf, 0x3a)
        relocations = {}
        for i in range(section_count):
            section = struct.unpack_from('<IIQQQQIIQQ', elf, section_offset + i * section_size)
            if section[1] != 4:  # SHT_RELA
                continue
            for at in range(section[4], section[4] + section[5], section[9]):
                address, info, addend = struct.unpack_from('<QQq', elf, at)
                if info & 0xffffffff == 8:  # R_X86_64_RELATIVE
                    relocations[address] = addend
        for n, record in enumerate(records):
            found = [row for row in rows if row[3] == record['name']]
            assert len(found) == 1
            start, size = [int(x, 16) for x in found[0][:2]]
            assembly = subprocess.check_output(['objdump', '-d', '-C', '--no-show-raw-insn', '-Mintel',
                                               f'--start-address={start}', f'--stop-address={start + size}', str(binary)], text=True)
            normalized, resolved = [], {}
            for line in assembly.splitlines():
                instruction = re.match(r'^\s*([0-9a-f]+):\s+(.*)$', line)
                if not instruction:
                    continue
                op = instruction[2]
                slot = re.search(r'#\s+([0-9a-f]+) <_DYNAMIC[^>]*>', op)
                if slot:
                    target = relocations[int(slot[1], 16)]
                    name = names[target]
                    resolved[slot[1]] = {'target': hex(target), 'name': name}
                    op = op[:slot.start()] + '# <' + name + '>'
                op = re.sub(r'\[rip[+-]0x[0-9a-f]+\]', '[rip+relocation]', op)
                op = re.sub(r'\b[0-9a-f]+ <', '<', op)
                normalized.append(f'{int(instruction[1], 16) - start:04x} {op}')
            normalized = '\n'.join(normalized) + '\n'
            record[variant] = {'start': hex(start), 'size': size, 'alignment_mod64': start % 64,
                               'normalized_sha256': sha(normalized.encode()),
                               'instruction_count': len(normalized.splitlines()), 'resolved_slots': resolved,
                               'normalized': normalized, 'assembly': assembly}
            (p / f'code-{n}-{variant}.txt').write_text(assembly)
            (p / f'normalized-{n}-{variant}.txt').write_text(normalized)
for record in records:
    record['normalized_equal'] = all(record[v]['normalized'] == record['before']['normalized'] for v in choices)
(p / 'code-comparison.json').write_text(json.dumps({
    'method': 'Compare instruction offsets and operations, remove link addresses from named calls and RIP references, and resolve anonymous GOT slots using ELF R_X86_64_RELATIVE relocations and symbol names. This checks selected function bodies, not the entire executable or runtime data placement.',
    'functions': records,
}, indent=2) + '\n')
for record in records:
    print(record['before']['instruction_count'], 'instructions; equal:', record['normalized_equal'], record['name'][:140])

scenario, address_mode, pair_count = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], int(sys.argv[3])
assert scenario in ['paired', 'same-before', 'same-after']
assert address_mode in ['normal', 'fixed', 'mixed']
case = sys.argv[4]
mode = 'subqueries' if case.endswith('_ansitrue') else 'generic-in'
suffix = 'subquery-check' if mode == 'subqueries' else 'check'
out = p / f'{case}-{left}-{right}-{scenario}-{address_mode}-{pair_count}'
out.mkdir()
load = lambda path: json.loads(Path(path).read_text())
canonical = {v: {r['id']: r for r in load(q / f'{"before" if binary_paths[v] == choices["accepted"] else "after"}-{suffix}.json')['results']} for v in ['before', 'after']}
env = os.environ.copy()
assert not any(k.startswith(('MALLOC_', 'GLIBC_', 'LD_PRELOAD', 'DECIMAL_BENCH_')) for k in env)
directions = [False, True] * (pair_count // 2)
assert len(directions) == pair_count
random.Random(88).shuffle(directions)
pairs = [(reverse, address_mode) for reverse in directions]
if address_mode == 'mixed':
    assert pair_count % 4 == 0
    pairs = [(False, 'normal'), (True, 'normal'), (False, 'fixed'), (True, 'fixed')] * (pair_count // 4)
    random.Random(88).shuffle(pairs)
binary_sha256 = {v: hashlib.sha256(binary_paths[v].read_bytes()).hexdigest() for v in ['before', 'after']}
runs = []
for pair, (reverse, run_address_mode) in enumerate(pairs):
    for label in (['after', 'before'] if reverse else ['before', 'after']):
        variant = label if scenario == 'paired' else scenario.removeprefix('same-')
        directory = out / f'{pair:02}-{label}'
        directory.mkdir()
        for name in ['control', 'ack']:
            os.mkfifo(directory / name)
        launch = ['taskset', '-c', '2']
        if run_address_mode == 'fixed':
            launch += ['setarch', 'x86_64', '-R']
        command = ['perf', 'stat', '--delay=-1',
                   f'--control=fifo:{directory}/control,{directory}/ack',
                   '--json-output', '-o', str(directory / 'counters.jsonl'), '-e',
                   '{instructions:u,cycles:u,branches:u,branch-misses:u},task-clock:u,context-switches:u,cpu-migrations:u,page-faults:u',
                   '--', *launch, str(binary_paths[variant]),
                   str(directory / 'capture.json'), mode, case]
        result = subprocess.run(command, env=env | {'DECIMAL_BENCH_PERF_DIR': str(directory),
                                'DECIMAL_BENCH_PERF_PHASE': 'execution', 'DECIMAL_BENCH_RETAIN': 'none'},
                                capture_output=True, text=True, check=True, timeout=180)
        capture = load(directory / 'capture.json')
        assert len(capture['results']) == (1 if mode == 'subqueries' else 2)
        for row in capture['results']:
            assert all(row[k] == v for k, v in canonical[variant][row['id']].items())
            if mode == 'subqueries':
                assert row['retention'] == 'none' and row['retained_rows'] == 0
        timed = capture['results'][0] if mode == 'subqueries' else next(r for r in capture['results'] if r['ansi'])
        assert len(timed['samples_ms']) == len(timed['planning_samples_ms']) == 9
        counters = [json.loads(line) for line in (directory / 'counters.jsonl').read_text().splitlines() if line.startswith('{')]
        assert len(counters) == 8 and all(c['pcnt-running'] == 100 for c in counters)
        assert result.stderr.count('Events enabled') == 1
        runs.append({'label': label, 'variant': variant, 'pair': pair, 'address_mode': run_address_mode, 'command': command,
                     'samples_ms': timed['samples_ms'], 'planning_samples_ms': timed['planning_samples_ms'],
                     'median_ms': statistics.median(timed['samples_ms']), 'counters': counters})
    (out / 'runs.json').write_text(json.dumps({'binary_sha256': binary_sha256, 'case': case, 'scenario': scenario, 'address_mode': address_mode,
                                            'pair_count': pair_count, 'pair_schedule': pairs, 'runs': runs}, indent=2) + '\n')
    print(scenario, address_mode, pair + 1, '/', pair_count, flush=True)

groups = {}
for label in ['before', 'after']:
    selected = [r for r in runs if r['label'] == label]
    assert len(selected) == pair_count
    groups[label] = {
        'process_medians_ms': [r['median_ms'] for r in selected],
        'median_ms': statistics.median(r['median_ms'] for r in selected),
        'median_counters': {event: statistics.median(float(next(c['counter-value'] for c in r['counters'] if c['event'] == event)) for r in selected)
                            for event in [c['event'] for c in selected[0]['counters']]},
    }
ratios = []
for pair in range(pair_count):
    rows = {r['label']: r for r in runs if r['pair'] == pair}
    ratios.append(100 * (rows['after']['median_ms'] / rows['before']['median_ms'] - 1))
rng = random.Random(88)
resampled = sorted(statistics.median(rng.choices(ratios, k=pair_count)) for _ in range(10000))
summary = {
    'groups': groups,
    'latency_change_pct': 100 * (groups['after']['median_ms'] / groups['before']['median_ms'] - 1),
    'paired_changes_pct': ratios,
    'median_paired_change_pct': statistics.median(ratios),
    'paired_median_bootstrap_95_percentile_interval': [resampled[249], resampled[9749]],
    'interval_note': 'Resample whole fresh-process pairs, not the nine within-process samples. This interval is conditional on this machine and run series.',
    'counter_changes_pct': {event: 100 * (groups['after']['median_counters'][event] / value - 1)
                            for event, value in groups['before']['median_counters'].items() if value != 0},
}
(out / 'summary.json').write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2) + '\n')
print(json.dumps(summary, indent=2), flush=True)

import datetime
import hashlib
import json
import random
import statistics
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

p = Path(__file__).parent
q = p.parent / 'float-in-zero-bool-a651e99'
root = Path('/home/hanbo/repo/delta-arrow-reader')
load = lambda file: json.loads(Path(file).read_text())
sha = lambda file: hashlib.sha256(Path(file).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
base = subprocess.check_output(['git', 'rev-parse', 'HEAD'], cwd=root, text=True).strip()
assert base.startswith('fad7088')
artifact = root / 'experiments/spark-sql/float-in-zero-bool-results.json'
prior = load(artifact)
builds = load(p / 'relink-builds.json')
control = load(p / 'control-build.json')
assert control['old_candidate'] == control['relinked_control'] == sha(p / 'control-bench') == sha(q / 'after-bench')
assert control['old_candidate'] == prior['provenance']['builds']['after']['binaries']['bench']
assert sha(builds['original_library']['path']) == builds['original_library']['sha256']
for alignment, record in builds['variants'].items():
    assert record['only_selected_section_alignment_changed'] and record['other_archive_members_identical']
    assert sha(p / f'align{alignment}/bench') == record['binary_sha256']
assert builds['variants']['16']['binary_sha256'] == control['relinked_control']
for kind in ['sources', 'executables']:
    for name, record in load(q / f'initial-{kind}.json').items():
        file = Path(record['path'])
        assert file.exists() == record.get('existed', True), name
        if file.exists():
            assert sha(file) == record['sha256'], name

checks = load(p / 'checks.json')
assert set(checks) == {'32', '64', '128', '256'}
assert sum(c['observations'] for cases in checks.values() for c in cases.values()) == 744
assert all(c['all_fields_identical'] for cases in checks.values() for c in cases.values())
code = load(p / 'code-comparison.json')['functions'][0]
assert code['normalized_equal']
layouts = {}
for variant in ['before', 'after', 'align32', 'align64', 'align128', 'align256']:
    row = code[variant]
    assert row['instruction_count'] == 127
    assert row['normalized_sha256'] == prior['selected_hot_loop_code']['functions'][0]['after']['normalized_sha256']
    start = int(row['start'], 16)
    layouts[variant] = {k: v for k, v in row.items() if k not in ['assembly', 'normalized']}
    layouts[variant].update(
        start_mod4096=start % 4096,
        lookup_loop_address=hex(start + 0xa0),
        row_loop_address=hex(start + 0x110),
        inner_loops_share_4k_page=(start + 0xa0) // 4096 == (start + 0x196 - 1) // 4096,
    )
assert [v for v, row in layouts.items() if row['inner_loops_share_4k_page']] == ['before', 'align128', 'align256']

known_binaries = {'accepted': sha(q / 'before-bench'), 'original': sha(p / 'control-bench')}
known_binaries |= {f'align{k}': v['binary_sha256'] for k, v in builds['variants'].items() if k != '16'}
series = {}
for file in sorted(p.glob('*/summary.json')):
    raw, summary = load(file.parent / 'runs.json'), load(file)
    assert all(digest in known_binaries.values() for digest in raw['binary_sha256'].values())
    assert len(raw['runs']) == raw['pair_count'] * 2
    for label in ['before', 'after']:
        runs = [r for r in raw['runs'] if r['label'] == label]
        medians = [statistics.median(r['samples_ms']) for r in runs]
        assert medians == summary['groups'][label]['process_medians_ms']
        assert statistics.median(medians) == summary['groups'][label]['median_ms']
        assert all(len(r['samples_ms']) == 9 for r in runs)
        assert all(len(r['counters']) == 8 and all(c['pcnt-running'] == 100 for c in r['counters']) for r in runs)
    ratios = []
    for pair in range(raw['pair_count']):
        rows = {r['label']: r for r in raw['runs'] if r['pair'] == pair}
        ratios.append(100 * (rows['after']['median_ms'] / rows['before']['median_ms'] - 1))
    assert ratios == summary['paired_changes_pct']
    assert statistics.median(ratios) == summary['median_paired_change_pct']
    rng = random.Random(88)
    bootstrap = sorted(statistics.median(rng.choices(ratios, k=len(ratios))) for _ in range(10000))
    assert [bootstrap[249], bootstrap[9749]] == summary['paired_median_bootstrap_95_percentile_interval']
    assert summary['latency_change_pct'] == 100 * (summary['groups']['after']['median_ms'] / summary['groups']['before']['median_ms'] - 1)
    series[file.parent.name] = raw | {'summary': summary}
assert len(series) == 16 and sum(len(s['runs']) for s in series.values()) == 480

scripts = {name: (p / name).read_text() for name in ['prepare.py', 'capture-link.py', 'build-control.py', 'relink.py', 'check.py', 'inspect-code.py', 'measure.py', 'report.py']}
for name, source in scripts.items():
    compile(source, name, 'exec')
spec = load(p / 'target-symbol.json')
measurements = [
    ['paired', 'normal', 16, 'generic_in_double_long_list', 'original', 'align32'],
    ['paired', 'normal', 16, 'generic_in_double_long_list', 'original', 'align64'],
    ['paired', 'normal', 16, 'generic_in_double_long_list', 'original', 'align256'],
    ['paired', 'normal', 16, 'generic_in_double_long_list', 'align64', 'align256'],
    ['paired', 'normal', 16, 'generic_in_double_long_list', 'accepted', 'align256'],
    ['paired', 'normal', 16, 'generic_in_double_long_list', 'original', 'align128'],
    ['paired', 'fixed', 16, 'generic_in_double_long_list', 'original', 'align256'],
    ['same-before', 'normal', 8, 'generic_in_double_long_list', 'original', 'align256'],
    ['same-after', 'normal', 8, 'generic_in_double_long_list', 'original', 'align256'],
] + [['paired', 'normal', 16, case, 'accepted', 'align256'] for case in [
    'float_compare_f32_ansitrue', 'generic_in_utf8_not_in', 'in_f64_long_ansitrue',
    'generic_in_float_zero_single', 'generic_in_double_zero_single',
    'float_in_dynamic_ansitrue', 'in_f64_dynamic_ansitrue',
]]
assert len(measurements) == len(series)
report = {

    'base_commit': base,
    'decision': 'Record a layout-sensitive regression, with no new Rust runtime or packaging change. A targeted section-alignment intervention removes the measured DOUBLE control gap in this build. The binary-specific alignment experiment is diagnostic and the native add-zero candidate remains outside the accepted optional sequence.',
    'scope': 'Reconstruct the exact previous candidate executable, then change only the alignment attribute of the object section containing the profiled Float64 IN loop and relink.     'summary': {
        'original_candidate_reproduced_byte_for_byte': True,
        'identity_roundtrip_alignment16': True,
        'distinct_layout_variants': 4,
        'correctness_captures': 744,
        'new_capture_differences_including_plans': 0,
        'timing_processes': 480,
        'normalized_hot_loop_instructions': 127,
        'all_selected_hot_loop_instructions_identical': True,
        'source_or_runtime_patch_adopted': False,
        'native_add_zero_adopted': False,
        'all_historical_performance_problems_resolved': False,
    },
    'provenance': {
        'prior_artifact': {'path': artifact.name, 'sha256': sha(artifact)},
        'control_build': control,
        'relinked_builds': builds,
        'binary_sha256': known_binaries,
        'target': {k: v for k, v in spec.items() if k != 'prior_code'},
        'original_object_sha256': sha(p / 'original.o'),
        'compiler_command': load(p / 'compile-command.json'),
        'linker_command_and_saved_objects': load(p / 'link-command.json'),
        'environment': {name: subprocess.check_output(command, text=True) for name, command in [
            ('rustc', ['rustc', '-Vv']), ('llvm_objcopy', ['llvm-objcopy', '--version']),
            ('cc', ['cc', '--version']), ('ar', ['ar', '--version']),
            ('perf', ['perf', '--version']), ('kernel', ['uname', '-srmo']), ('cpu', ['lscpu'])]},
        'shared_sources_locks_executables_and_original_library_verified_unchanged': True,
    },
    'correctness': {
        'layout_captures': checks,
        'reference': 'Each changed layout matches all 74 generic and 112 older benchmark captures from the prior candidate exactly, including output metadata and physical plans. The alignment-16 roundtrip is byte-identical to that candidate. No fresh Spark comparison, planner compilation, Arrow unit-test run or full 6332-observation replay is needed for this diagnostic relink; the Rust code is unchanged.',
    },
    'code_placement': {
        'method': 'Input object sections have identical payloads, symbols, relocations and attributes except the one selected section alignment. All other archive members are byte-identical. Relinked loop instructions are compared after resolving named relocations. Full normalized instruction text is retained in the preceding artifact.',
        'variants': layouts,
        'observation': 'The baseline, alignment-128 and alignment-256 binaries place the two hot inner loops in the same 4 KiB virtual page. Original, alignment-32 and alignment-64 split them across a page boundary. Alignment 128 still leaves the function prologue in the preceding page. Code placement changes elsewhere in the binary can also result from relinking.',
